subject: Observability processor consolidation — routing / DPA checklist
messages:
From: Julian Park <julian.park@logstream.example>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:40 -0700
Subject: Notice — consolidation of observability processors and routing change

Hi Nikhil —

Quick heads up from LogStream: over the next 6 weeks we're consolidating our observability processing (metrics/logs/trace enrichment) for a subset of customers onto a single processing cluster to improve performance. For Redwood accounts in scope this will move event processing that currently runs in our Frankfurt cluster to our primary US ingestion tier.

Key points: 
- Affected data: delivery logs, span metadata, and anonymized service metadata (no PII by our current understanding).
- New processors: log-enrich-v2 (US) and metrics-aggregator-v3 (US).
- Expected cutover window: 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-15 (tentative).
- We will use a dedicated KMS key in our US region for post-processing; keys will remain under LogStream control.

Attached: consolidation-implementation-plan.pdf (high-level timeline + technical diagram).

Action requested from Redwood: please confirm whether you need: 1) a DPA addendum for subprocessor change, 2) evidence of encryption in transit/at rest and 3) confirmation of any contractual export-control constraints that would block EU->US routing.

I'll be available this week for a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Julian Park
Partner Ops — LogStream Inc.

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Julian Park <julian.park@logstream.example>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice — consolidation of observability processors and routing change

Julian —

Thanks for the heads up and the plan. A few clarifying questions before we share this with our legal/compliance reviewers: 

1) Data scope: you note no PII — can you confirm whether any free-text payloads (application logs) that could contain customer-controlled PII will be processed? If so, we need examples and redaction/retention controls.
2) KMS: can you confirm key ownership and whether Redwood can request key access logs per our DPA? Also include the KMS region and whether keys rotate automatically.
3) Subprocessor roster: please provide a list of downstream subprocessors involved during ingestion and enrichment for the new US processors (names, countries, roles).
4) Cross-border flow: we need a simple dataflow diagram and a note on retention periods post-processing.

We'll triage internally but broadly: if data crosses from EU to US we will likely need a DPA addendum and an update to our subprocessor registry. Please attach any SOC2 report references and the implementation diagram in the next message.

Proposed next steps:
- Please send the downstream subprocessor list and the KMS details by EOD Thu 2026-06-11.
- If you can share SOC2 references and the implementation diagram that will speed Legal's review.

I'm looping in Kimberly and Laura from Procurement/Legal and Soojin from Infosec for routing/export checks.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, Julian Park <julian.park@logstream.example>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 14:27:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice — consolidation of observability processors and routing change

Nikhil / team —

Thanks, Julian — appreciate the notice. From a procurement perspective this is not an automatic blocker but we need three things before approval to proceed: 

1) Downstream subprocessor inventory (name, country, role, whether they handle persisted copies).
2) Confirmation that any free-text logs are redacted or can be excluded by the customer. If not, we need retention limits and the option to opt-out.
3) Export-control check for EU customers — Soojin, can you validate whether any customers in scope would require data residency constraints?

Let's tentatively target a response to LogStream by Fri 2026-06-12 so they have time to adjust cutover. If Legal needs a formal DPA addendum we'll route a template.

K —
Kimberly Park
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Julian Park <julian.park@logstream.example>, nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice — consolidation of observability processors and routing change

Julian / Nikhil / team —

Thank you for the advance notification. From Legal's side we require the following before we can sign off: 

• A completed subprocessor addendum (we can use our standard template) or a DPA amendment signed by LogStream. I have attached a draft template for your reference (dpa-amendment-template.docx).
• The downstream subprocessor roster and evidence of SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) for each subprocessor that will access or persist customer logs.
• Confirmation on whether Redwood's customers will be able to opt-out of the EU->US cutover (e.g., opt to keep processing in Frankfurt).

Please provide these items by 2026-06-12 so we can expedite review. If LogStream prefers a short SLA carve-out form for impacted customers instead of a full amendment, indicate that in your reply.

cc: Soojin for InfoSec validation on encryption and export controls.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.
